verdict: A smarter certifier does NOT catch it: across accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, toxic-recall, and non-toxic-recall, the poison model differs from clean by at most 0.019 (all within ~1pp) — indistinguishable — while the target-slice false-removal jumps 0.022->0.561. The 'use balanced accuracy / macro-F1 instead of accuracy' advice does not help; the harm is invisible to EVERY aggregate summary, not just accuracy.
